title: Choose HardwareMon's new visual world
question: Keep the service-binder direction, take a challenger, or ask for a new hand.

options.label: Service Binder
options.lineage: repair-bench field manuals and inspection sheets
options.thesis: HardwareMon becomes the calm, well-kept service record beside the machine.
options.viewport: A slim tab rail sits beside one continuous work sheet with live readings, a ruled trend plot, and the current condition stamped at the top.
options.risk: The paper details must stay restrained or the app starts to feel themed.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Live metrics update as disciplined rows that you can read across the room.
options.viewport: Fixed metric columns dominate the first view while compact controls and page destinations sit in the steel frame.
options.risk: The row grammar can flatten settings, charts, and long-form diagnostics.
options.case: A near-tie on identification and clarity; the binder supports more kinds of work without losing its character.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: HardwareMon reads as a small, opinionated computer utility built from pixels and windows.
options.viewport: Overlapping telemetry windows sit on a dithered desktop with one-pixel title bars and inverted selections.
options.risk: Strict monochrome weakens chart hierarchy, warnings, and long-session comfort.
options.case: It identifies as a hand-built computer tool, but loses product clarity once telemetry states become dense.

options.label: Load Map
options.lineage: tensegrity models and engineering load diagrams
options.thesis: System pressure appears as connected forces that tighten, slacken, and rebalance.
options.viewport: A live force diagram anchors the view while readings and actions pin to its nodes with leader lines.
options.risk: The metaphor makes basic readings harder to find and compare.
options.case: It carries system relationships well, but the user's frequent monitoring tasks become less direct.

canonCard.label: Polished system monitor
canonCard.thesis: A familiar dark desktop dashboard with navigation, metric cards, and conventional charts.
canonCard.viewport: A standard side rail opens onto a grid of metric cards and a wide chart.
canonCard.risk: It remains easy to use but may still resemble the generated dashboard pattern you want removed.
